item.title: See Conversions
item.description: I recently1 stumbled across an interesting C function. The function was quite simple–just a few lines long—so I was sure I understood it. And yet, the function produced unexpected results—and I could not understand why. Debugging this tiny function led me down the dark hole that is implicit type conversions in C. I have reproduced the function in its entirety below (with a 2-line modification to make the output more readable for this post).

item.title: Four Years and Beyond
item.description:
I originally kicked off this blog around April 2022. It’s now February 2026 and nearly four years (a.k.a one quadrennium1) have passed. How has this blog progressed?

  • I published 3 posts (including this one).
  • I authored 9 draft posts (defined as an unpublished post over 300 words with an average/median word count of ~2000/2300 words).
  • I sketched out 9 post ideas (defined as an unpublished post with 300 words or less).

If I also count unpublished draft posts, then my average post output over the past four years is 3 posts/year.

item.title: Learning Haskell
item.description:
TLDR: In this blog post, I list some of the challenges that I faced while learning Haskell. Skip down to Challenges to see my list.

My journey to Haskell dates back to the start of my university days. I first heard about Haskell from an older grad student I worked with. He was an opinionated man with an impressively long beard who rolled his own cigarettes and often took smoke breaks just outside the department building. Haskell was a challenging and mind-bending language, he promised, as a puff of smoke wafted into the air.

item.title: Directed Steps
item.description:
Ground Rules and Goals

Welcome aboard my new blog srs.fyi! Do mind your step.

The purpose of this blog is two-fold, in order of importance:

  1. to record my musings and learnings;
  2. to share my thoughts with others.

While we’re here, let’s take care of some other housekeeping items:

  • Scope: the scope of the blog includes anything that catches my interest, though I expect most posts to be technically oriented and related to my academic and professional interests.
  • Schedule: the blog will have no schedule; I will write things as they come, at their own pace.
  • Ads: this blog will have no ads or affiliate links (though I may link to things that I like just because I like them).
